## What Is a Latent Field?

:::: {.columns .col-center-container}
::: {.column .v-center width="50%"}
- **Latent:** Not directly measurable.
- **Field:** intensity or properties can vary throughout space and or time.
- e.g., temperature
:::
::: {.column .v-center width="50%"}
![Temperature Field](assets:2026_latent_human_influence/temperature_field_volume.webp){.img-card fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

---

## Latent Human Influence Field (LHIF)

:::: {.columns .col-center-container}
::: {.column .v-center width="50%"}
- **Latent:** human influence is inferred from its traces.
- **Field:** influence can vary across the sediment archive (translated into time).
- many proxies are noisy observations of a shared LHIF.
- Proxy records differ in resolution, distribution, and measurement structure.
- Joint inference needs a model linking observations to a shared process.
:::
::: {.column .v-center width="50%"}
![Theoretical LHIF](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0305440326001937-gr1.jpg){.img-card fig-align="center"}
:::
::::

## Site and Context

Cannonically, Koh Ker was established by Jayavarman IV in 921 CE. It became the sole capital of the Khmer Empire from 928–944 CE, before the political centre returned to Angkor. The site represents a brief but highly distinctive phase of Khmer urbanism, monumental architecture, and sculpture.

![Koh Ker in Regional Context](assets:2026_latent_human_influence/kk_regional.jpeg){.img-card height=600 fig-align="center"}

::: notes
Add the paper's site map. Outline the historical context and distinguish political history from the sedimentary evidence for local activity.
:::

- Bayesian hierarchical latent-variable model.
- Proxy channels linked within a causal framework.
- Depth-wise reconstructions for the pilot trenches.

## Ceramics Channel

Ceramics channel across all 8 trenches. The model captures the depth-wise variation in ceramic abundance, which serves as a proxy for human activity. The Latent influence field is inferred from the ceramics data, showing peaks corresponding to periods of increased human activity.

![Ceramics Comparison](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0305440326001937-gr6.jpg){fig-align="center" height="600" .img-card}

::: notes
Use the paper's comparison to explain the practical value of susceptibility measurements. Discuss what the pilot establishes about this proxy at Koh Ker.
:::

---

## Magnetic Susceptibility Channel

Magnetic susceptibility channel across all 8 trenches. The model captures the depth-wise variation in magnetic susceptibility, which serves as a proxy for human activity. The Latent influence field is inferred from the magnetic susceptibility data, showing peaks corresponding to periods of increased human activity.

![Magnetic Susceptibility Comparison](https://ars.els-cdn.com/content/image/1-s2.0-S0305440326001937-gr7.jpg){fig-align="center" height="600" .img-card}

::: notes

## Pinhole Sampling

At the moment, we have a "pinhole" view of the latent human influence field at Koh Ker. The pilot trenches provide depth-wise reconstructions, but spatial coverage is limited. Future work could expand trenching and sampling to better understand the spatial distribution of human influence across the site.

![Pinhole Sampling](assets:2026_latent_human_influence/lhif_pinhole.webp){fig-align="center" height="600" .img-card}
